article_title: Beyond China's humanoid robots, a quieter machine revolution is unfolding

tasks.prompt: What is the article's central argument?
options: China's robot strategy is limited to entertainment spectacles
China has stopped training people for technical jobs
The less glamorous spread of industrial automation may matter more than attention-grabbing humanoid robots
Chinese factories are replacing robots with manual labour
tasks.correct_answer: The less glamorous spread of industrial automation may matter more than attention-grabbing humanoid robots
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הטענה המרכזית היא שהמהפכה המשמעותית אינה רק ברובוטים דמויי אדם שמושכים תשומת לב, אלא בהתפשטות השקטה והרחבה של אוטומציה תעשייתית במפעלים.

tasks.prompt: How does teacher Chen Tianyu keep his robotics lessons current?
options: He spends spare time visiting factories that are moving towards automation
He studies only historical machines in museums
He asks students to avoid industrial sites
He teaches from one unchanged textbook
tasks.correct_answer: He spends spare time visiting factories that are moving towards automation
tasks.explanation_hebrew: צ'ן טיאניו מבקר בזמנו הפנוי במפעלים העוברים לאוטומציה, כדי לדעת אילו נושאים וכישורים לתעדף בהוראה.

tasks.prompt: What scale of industrial automation does the article report in China?
options: About 30 robots, all at one college
Fewer than 20,000 robots nationwide
Exactly one million humanoid robots in homes
More than two million robots working in factories
tasks.correct_answer: More than two million robots working in factories
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה מציינת שבמפעלי סין עובדים יותר משני מיליון רובוטים — יותר מבכל מדינה אחרת.

tasks.prompt: What is one purpose of the large vocational institutes described in the article?
options: To train students only in traditional calligraphy
To produce a new generation of engineers able to program, operate and maintain advanced machines
To prevent young people from entering factories
To display robots without allowing students to use them
tasks.correct_answer: To produce a new generation of engineers able to program, operate and maintain advanced machines
tasks.explanation_hebrew: המוסדות המקצועיים נועדו להכשיר דור חדש של עובדים ומהנדסים בעלי כישורים בתכנות, הפעלה ותחזוקה של רובוטים ומערכות מתקדמות.

tasks.prompt: What does “meticulously” suggest about how China is building its robotic future?
options: It is happening accidentally and without planning
It is being hidden from every factory worker
It is being planned and developed with great care and attention to detail
It is progressing only through private hobbies
tasks.correct_answer: It is being planned and developed with great care and attention to detail
tasks.explanation_hebrew: meticulously פירושו בקפדנות רבה ובתשומת לב לפרטים; המילה מדגישה שהמהלך מתוכנן ומפותח באופן שיטתי.

tasks.prompt: What is a “looming” gap in the workforce?
options: A gap that existed only in ancient history
A gap that has already been fully solved
A small difference in workers' uniforms
A shortage that is approaching and causing concern
tasks.correct_answer: A shortage that is approaching and causing concern
tasks.explanation_hebrew: looming מתאר דבר המתקרב ומעורר דאגה. כאן מדובר במחסור עתידי בעובדים עקב אוכלוסייה מצטמצמת ומזדקנת.

tasks.prompt: Give two examples of how China is preparing people and industry for wider automation.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לציין שתי דוגמאות קונקרטיות מן הכתבה, רצוי אחת מתחום ההכשרה ואחת מתחום התעשייה או המדיניות.
expected_points: Vocational institutes teach coding, AI and robotics
Students program industrial robots and develop robotic medical instruments
Teachers visit automated factories to keep training relevant
Factories are installing robots at extraordinary scale
The government is backing innovation with a roughly $20bn plan
Workers are being trained to operate or maintain machines

tasks.prompt: Why might industrial robots have a greater near-term impact than humanoid prototypes?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להשוות בין שימוש תעשייתי קיים לבין אב־טיפוס ראוותני ולהסביר את ההסקה על בסיס הכתבה.
expected_points: Industrial robots already number more than two million in Chinese factories
They perform practical repetitive production tasks now
Robot arms can be tailored to specific factory needs
Humanoid demonstrations attract attention but many remain prototypes
Industrial automation can affect productivity and employment across many sectors

tasks.prompt: Summarise the forces driving China's automation push and the uncertainties it creates.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכתוב סיכום אנליטי באנגלית הכולל מניעים, אמצעי יישום ולפחות סיכון או שאלה פתוחה אחת.
expected_points: China wants to compete at the forefront of global technological innovation
A shrinking and ageing population creates a looming labour gap
Factories are rapidly installing industrial robots
Vocational schools are training workers for robotics and AI
Automation may raise productivity in a sluggish economy
The transition can displace jobs and requires retraining
Machines also require maintenance, inspection and repair
The speed and management of the transition will shape its social impact

tasks.prompt: Write a short, balanced response to the claim that factory automation will simply eliminate human workers.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכתוב תגובה מאוזנת באנגלית הכוללת ראיות מן הכתבה הן לסיכון התעסוקתי והן לצורך המתמשך בכישורי אדם.
expected_points: Robots can replace some repetitive tasks
Rapid automation may eliminate or transform existing jobs
A shrinking workforce gives factories a practical reason to automate
People are still needed to program, operate, inspect and repair machines
Vocational education can help workers move into new roles
The speed of transition and access to retraining are crucial
